prompt: Vertical 9:16 editorial advertising photograph, a jewellery close-up of the necklace's clasp for its listing: a close crop of one woman's nape at night, the camera directly behind her head and a little above it, looking down at about 20 degrees. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy its construction exactly and ignore its background and light. Reference 2 is a detail of the same piece. The clasp is posed exactly as in reference 2: the straight bar lies across the upper left of the ring with its row of tiny stones facing the camera, the ring sits below it, and the spring gate with its small push-pin nub and ribbed collar sits at the right. Reference 2 is a much closer view than this picture: copy its construction and pose, never its framing or its size. Build it exactly: a 50 cm chain, 4 mm wide, of elongated paperclip links (about 4 x 11 mm) in polished 18k gold tone; 1 thick round spring-gate sailor ring about 22 mm across (about 14 mm opening, small push-pin nub, ribbed gate collar) and 1 short straight bar about 15 mm long set with 1 row of about 9 tiny clear stones, on a jump ring. No pendant, no other stones. Must stay a sailor ring with a straight bar 0.6-0.7x the ring, never a plain donut ring, a lobster clasp, or a curved or multi-row pave bar. The chain has exactly two ends, and both are at the clasp: the left end is joined to the outer end of the bar by the bar's one jump ring, and the right end is joined to the ring by the one jump ring around its barrel collar beside the gate. Exactly one strand of chain leaves the clasp on each side and runs around that side of her neck. Nothing else is attached to or touches the ring: no link, no chain end and no jump ring at its left side, its bottom or anywhere except the barrel collar. Last time a third, extra strand of chain came around the left of her neck and ended in a loose jump ring touching the ring's left edge: that strand does not exist. Keep reference 2's gate exactly: the flat tube end and the thin gate across the top of the ring, the barrel collar at about 1 o'clock carrying the right chain's jump ring, the push-pin nub at 3 o'clock pointing outward, the ribbed grooves at 4 o'clock. Do not redesign, restyle, resize or add anything. SCENE: the instant the clasp has been closed, before the hands let go. The nape and upper back of an Indian woman of about sixty, seen from directly behind, her head bowed a little forward the way one bows while someone fastens a necklace: grey-streaked black hair pinned in a low bun with a plain black band, the top edge of the picture cutting through the bun; fine soft hairs at the nape; the rounded Peter Pan collar of a faded, dusty rose cotton nightie at the bottom, in deep shadow, darker than her skin and never bright or saturated (last time it came out as a bright rose crew-neck T-shirt: never a T-shirt). The clasp has been turned to the back and rests flat on the skin at the base of her nape, with a band of bare skin about three ring-widths deep between it and the nightie's collar, closed exactly as in reference 2. Two younger hands (a woman of about thirty-five, light wheatish skin, short nails with chipped coral polish, five fingers each with correct anatomy, no rings, no bangles, no watch) come in from the top edge, the forearms falling into soft shadow either side of the bun, still at work: the left thumb and forefinger rest lightly on the chain where it lies on her skin, two links to the left of the bar's jump ring, and the right forefinger rests on the chain two links to the right of the ring's barrel collar, both about to let go; no part of the chain is lifted off her skin. No finger covers the ring, its gate, its nub, the bar or its stones. The paperclip links run from the clasp around both sides of her neck and out of sight. SCALE, the most important instruction: the necklace is fine against the body. The ring is about as wide as two paperclip links laid end to end; the back of her neck is about five ring-widths wide (about 11 cm), never four, never three; the field of view is about 12 cm, so the ring spans about a fifth of the frame width and the bar about two thirds of the ring; each side shows about five paperclip links between the clasp and the side of her neck. The ring and the bar touch the skin with a soft, true contact shadow under them, the chain lies on the skin with its own fine shadow, and the fingertips leave true contact shadows on the chain. The daughter's hands are adult hands at true scale beside the 22 mm ring: each fingertip is about 15 mm wide, about two thirds of the ring's width, never slender or child-sized fingers beside a large ring (last time her fingers were drawn too slender, so the ring looked too big beside them). COMPOSITION: the top edge of the picture cuts through the bun, so only its lower half shows and there is no crown of the head in frame. The clasp's centre sits 42 percent of the way down the frame and about 55 percent across, never lower than 45 percent (last time it sat almost 60 percent down: lift it). The nightie's collar begins about 62 percent down. The top 30 percent is the dark lower bun and the shadowed forearms, for a headline. The left quarter below the left hand, from 45 percent down, is calm shadowed skin, for a column of type. Everything below 60 percent falls into deep cocoa shadow, for a card. LIGHT: a warm tungsten bedside lamp from the right, soft, falling off fast; one small hard specular kicker from above left draws a crisp bright line along the curve of the ring and the bar and puts a pinpoint catchlight in each tiny stone: small sharp points of light, never rays, never star-shaped glints. GRADE: deep warm cocoa and umber, near-monochrome; the 18k gold tone is the only bright, saturated thing, the warm-neutral yellow of reference 1, never orange, copper or brassy. The nightie stays in deep shadow, darker than her skin and never bright or saturated; the lamp lights only the nape, the hands and the clasp. Natural film grain, believable imperfection, the hush of an Indian home at night. No face, no profile, no cheek, no jaw, no eyes, no eyebrows. No water, no droplets. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no printing on anything. One product only: no earrings, no other jewellery.
